lines.trans: Good morning, Madam Carmen! Look what arrived at our gate last night.
My suitcase! I am going to open the top pocket... yes, my red ribbon!
And your cup inside? Is it still in one piece?
Not a single crack! Who brought it back?
We do not know. Someone left it on the step and rang the bell.
And he did not ask for his own suitcase with the wooden train?
He left a short note asking us to keep it until Friday.
How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt very familiar to me.
Really? Do you know someone in Valencia?
Twenty-five years ago I taught piano near here, though memories fade.
For now, his suitcase stays safe under lock and key.
Wonderful! Now I am ready for a big breakfast.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.
Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.trans: I am heading there right now.
Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.
Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Single word meaning 'last night' (never la última noche).

examples.text: Anoche llovió mucho en la ciudad.
examples.trans: Last night it rained heavily in the city.
Did you sleep well last night?

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Coat or trouser pocket.

examples.trans: The pocket is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bolsillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pockets from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Borro la nota vieja con goma.
examples.trans: I erase the old note with a rubber.

examples.text: La lluvia borró la tiza de la pizarra.
examples.trans: The rain washed the chalk off the board.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Cerca de + noun = near something; de cerca = up close.

examples.trans: My family lives very nearby.
Look closely at this page.

meanings.note: Silk ribbon or adhesive tape.

examples.trans: The ribbon is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cintas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ribbons from the door.

meanings.note: Dar clase de piano = to teach piano lessons.

examples.trans: The lesson is here.

examples.text: Vemos las clases desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lessons from the door.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

conocer.gloss: to know (a person or place); to meet

meanings.en: to know (a person or place); to meet
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg conozco; preterite conocí often means 'met for the first time'.

examples.trans: I know this neighbourhood very well.
Yesterday we met the new neighbour.

meanings.note: Opposite of largo (long).

examples.trans: It is a short piece.

examples.text: Dejó una nota corta pidiendo guardarla hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: He left a short note asking us to keep it until Friday.

meanings.note: Describes either an inquisitive person or an intriguing detail.

examples.trans: It is a curious piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué curioso! La letra de esa etiqueta me resultaba muy familiar.
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt very familiar to me.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.trans: There are four tables inside.
I will be back in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Sigue entera = it is still in one piece.

examples.trans: It is a whole piece.
And your cup inside? Is it still in one piece?

meanings.note: Single step of a staircase (plural: escalones).

examples.trans: The step is here.

examples.text: Vemos los escalones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the steps from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Luggage tag or bottle label.

examples.trans: The tag is here.

examples.text: Vemos las etiquetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tags from the door.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.trans: It is a family piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué curioso! La letra de esa etiqueta me resultaba muy familiar.
examples.trans: How curious! The handwriting on that tag felt very familiar to me.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

meanings.note: Crack in a wall, ceiling, or tile.

examples.trans: The crack is here.

examples.text: Vemos las grietas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cracks from the door.

meanings.note: Past-participle adjective from guardar.

examples.trans: It is a kept safe piece.

examples.text: De momento, su maleta sigue guardada bajo llave.
examples.trans: For now, his suitcase stays safe under lock and key.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.
She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.
How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Tu letra means 'your handwriting'.

examples.trans: The handwriting is here.

examples.text: Vemos las letras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the handwritings from the door.

meanings.note: With estar, means 'ready / all set'; with ser, means 'smart'.

examples.text: El té caliente ya está listo.
examples.trans: The hot tea is ready now.
She is a very smart architect.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: llegué.

examples.trans: I always arrive ten minutes early.

examples.text: El tren de Madrid llegó en punto.
examples.trans: The train from Madrid arrived on the dot.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.
See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Warm praise.

examples.trans: It is a wonderful piece.

examples.text: ¡Maravilloso! Ahora estoy lista para un gran desayuno.
examples.trans: Wonderful! Now I am ready for a big breakfast.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: pido, pidió).

examples.text: Pido un café con leche, por favor.
examples.trans: I will order a coffee with milk, please.

examples.text: El cartero me pidió una firma.
examples.trans: The postman asked me for a signature.

meanings.note: Core contrast conjunction.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera, pero dentro se está bien.
examples.trans: It is cold outside, yet inside it is cosy.

examples.text: Es pequeño, pero tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: It is small, but it has lots of light.

meanings.note: Tocar el piano = to play the piano.

examples.trans: The piano is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pianos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pianos from the door.

meanings.note: Mi propia maleta = my own suitcase.

examples.trans: It is an own piece.

examples.text: ¿Y no pidió su propia maleta con el tren de madera?
examples.trans: And he did not ask for his own suitcase with the wooden train?

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose blue suitcase is this?

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Viejos recuerdos = old memories.

examples.trans: The memory is here.

examples.text: Vemos los recuerdos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the memorys from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El viaje en tren resultó muy cómodo.
examples.trans: The train ride turned out very comfortable.
The new recipe turns out super easy.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.trans: It is a red piece.

examples.text: ¡Dígales que la mía tiene una cinta roja en el bolsillo de arriba!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

saber.gloss: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)

meanings.en: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)
meanings.note: Irregular: sé, supe; sabe igual que = it tastes just like.

examples.trans: Do you know where the wrench is?

examples.text: Este bizcocho sabe a limón fresco.
examples.trans: This cake tastes of fresh lemon.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.text: Sigue todo recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead to the bridge.
Is the water still hot?

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

meanings.note: Tocar el timbre = ring the bell.

examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos los timbres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: Irregular: traigo, traje; future traeré.

examples.text: Ahora mismo le traigo una cuchara.
examples.trans: I will bring you a spoon right now.
Yesterday she brought flowers from the market.

meanings.note: Plural los trenes.

examples.trans: The train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trains from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Numbers 21–29 are written as one word in Spanish.

examples.trans: That happened twenty-five years ago.
There are twenty-five chairs in total.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

vuelta.gloss: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)

meanings.en: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)
meanings.note: Dar una vuelta = take a stroll / make one turn.

examples.trans: The turn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vueltas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the turns from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.
